## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR deletes `app/defaults.json` while `load_defaults` still reads it, so that call fails, and this must be fixed before merge. It also has two smaller problems: `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535, and `load_config` silently returns `{}` on any error.

## Changes
The PR adds three helpers to `app/parse.py`: `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (which can use ujson), and `normalize_host`. It also lets `parse_timeout` accept a millisecond (`ms`) suffix, adds tests for the new code, adds two docs/fixture files, and deletes `app/defaults.json`.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json or update load_defaults — `app/startup.py:6` still runs `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`, and the deleted file is the only thing it reads. With the file gone, every call to `load_defaults()` raises `FileNotFoundError`. — Any startup path that calls `load_defaults()` crashes instead of getting the `{"timeout":30}` defaults. — Fix: Keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `load_defaults` and its callers in the same PR so they no longer need it.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 in is_valid_port — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` because `0 < p < 65535` excludes the upper bound, but the docstring promises "a usable TCP port (1-65535)". `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` only checks 0, 1 and 8080. — Configs that use port 65535 are wrongly rejected, and no test protects the upper bound. — Fix: Use `0 < p <= 65535` and add a 65535/65536 case to `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound`.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — load_config swallows every error and returns {} — A missing file, a permission error or malformed JSON all hit `except Exception: return {}`, with no log or signal to the caller. The docstring "Load the JSON config at path." does not mention this fallback either. — Operators with a typo in the config path or a broken JSON file get default settings without being told, which makes misconfiguration hard to diagnose. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` for the default case and let parse errors raise; otherwise log the path and exception, and document the fallback in the docstring.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Make normalize_host's empty-input docstring match the code — The docstring says "returns None when h is empty", but `if h == "": return ""` returns an empty string. — Callers that follow the docstring and check `is None` will treat an empty host as a real value.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Test normalize_host's trailing-dot branch — No test covers the `lowered.endswith(".")` strip; `test_normalize_host_lowercases` only passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot. — If the FQDN-suffix handling breaks, no test will catch it. — Fix: Add a case such as `"Example.COM."` to `test_normalize_host_lowercases`.
